ai_coaching_notes.message: You've got everything you need.

500m: You're off to a cracking start, tour! At 0.5 kilometres in, you’re clocking a solid pace of 5 minutes and 5 seconds per kilometre. Your heart rate at 131 beats per minute is spot on for that aerobic zone. Keep it steady and enjoy the rhythm of your run!

HR: Hey there, Tour! You're cruising at 141 bpm in Zone 3, which is grand for a tempo run, but don’t be tempted to burn out like a candle in the wind! Keep that pace steady and save a bit of gas for the finish line; you’ll thank yourself later!

Cadence: You're currently at a cadence of 156 steps per minute, which is quite a bit below your target of 175 steps per minute. Let's focus on quickening that foot turnover! Think about picking your feet up lighter and faster, like you're tapping to a beat. You'll feel more efficient and reduce impact stress.

Km 1: Brilliant start, Tour! You've just completed the first kilometre at a split pace of 5 minutes and 13 seconds per kilometre. That's a cracking pace, especially considering it's 27 seconds per kilometre faster than your average! Keep this momentum going—your current cadence is looking good!

HR: Looking grand at 140 bpm in Zone 3, but remember, you don’t want to be sprinting up a hill like a mad hare just yet! Steady it down a notch, and let’s save those speedy legs for when the finish line is in sight!

Technique (feet_cadence): Let’s pick up the pace on those feet! Your current cadence is at 166 steps per minute. Aim for a quicker tempo, around 170 to 180 steps per minute. Think of light, bouncy steps as you push through this distance. You’ve got it, Tour!

HR: Hey, Tour! You're cruising at a cheeky 149 bpm in Zone 3 — mighty effort! Just remember, it’s a bit like trying to bake a cake: you don’t want to rush it. Slow it down a tad to keep the icing nice and smooth, and save some energy for the finish!

Km 2: Brilliant effort on that last split! You clocked a split pace of 5 minutes and 52 seconds per kilometer while descending a steep 13.1% grade. Remember, it’s tough on the legs, but you’re tackling it like a champ! Keep an eye on your cadence; it’s currently at 154 steps per minute, which is spot on. Keep pushing through!

Cadence: Alright, you’re currently at a cadence of 153 steps per minute, which is a bit shy of your optimal target of 162 steps per minute. Let’s focus on quickening that turnover! Think about driving your arms a bit more to help lift your legs and bring your foot strike closer to your body. Keep it light and snappy! You’ve got this!

Technique (recovery_arm_shakeout): Let’s shake off that tension! With your heart rate at 142 beats per minute, it’s time to drop your arms and give them a quick shake for about ten seconds. Loosen them up, feel the release, and then reset your form. This will help you regain that fluidity as you tackle the remaining distance!

HR: Alright, Tour! At 140 bpm in Zone 3, you're cruising along like a speedy little hare — just don’t forget the tortoise's wisdom! Keep that heart rate in check to save some energy for the finish line; you'll want to feel grand, not like you’ve run a marathon in a sprint! 🐢🏃‍♂️

HR: Look at you, cruising at 141 bpm in Zone 3 — mighty fine tempo! Just remember, if you keep this pace too long, you might turn into a human steam train, so sprinkle in a bit of recovery before you hit the hills again, grand?

Pace Trend: You're noticing a gradual slowdown, now at 6 minutes and 19 seconds per kilometer. Let’s tighten up your form! Roll your shoulders back and relax them; keep your arms driving forward. This will help you regain that rhythm. You want to aim for something closer to your average of 6 minutes and 3 seconds per kilometer! Let's pick it up!

Cadence: Right now, let's focus on boosting that cadence! You're currently at 120 steps per minute, but your target is 148 steps per minute. Think about lifting your knees a bit more and tapping your feet down quicker — imagine a rhythm that feels light and bouncy. You’ve got this!

HR: Fair play, you're holding steady at 143 bpm in Zone 3 – mighty effort! Just remember, if you start feeling like you're wrestling a bear, it might be time to ease off a tad to keep that tempo smooth and breezy. Keep it grand!

Technique (pacing_even_distribution): Let’s lock in that pacing! You’re currently at six minutes and thirty-seven seconds per kilometer, and it’s time to focus on your form. As you descend, keep your torso upright and your arms relaxed but purposeful. Imagine your legs are like pistons—driving you forward with each step, maintaining that smooth rhythm. You’ve got this!

Km 3: You're powering through a steep climb at a 10.6% grade! Your split pace is currently 7 minutes and 4 seconds per kilometer. This tough terrain can slow you down, so keep your focus and take those steps steady. You're doing brilliantly!

HR: Great job, Tour! You're cruising at 129 bpm in Zone 2, which is as comfy as a warm cup of tea on a rainy day. Keep that steady pace — think of it as a gentle stroll through the park, rather than a mad dash to the pub!

Km 4: Alright, tour! You've just completed kilometer 4 with a split pace of 7 minutes and 8 seconds per kilometer. It looks like you're easing off a bit on a climb here, but your heart rate at 143 beats per minute shows you’re still pushing through! 

Keep it up! You're doing well overall, but let's aim to find that rhythm again!

Technique (mental_visualisation): Alright, let’s lock in! Picture yourself crossing that finish line strong, feeling every ounce of power in your legs. You've conquered three point two kilometres, so imagine your best form and run toward that image. With your heart rate at 130 beats per minute, let's channel that energy into a smooth, confident stride!

HR: Well done, Tour! You're chugging along at a grand 126 bpm in Zone 2—just the right pace to chat with a mate while building that aerobic engine. Keep it steady and don’t let those legs get too eager; remember, we're in this for the long haul, not a sprint to the pub!

Technique (breathing_rhythm): Focus on syncing your breath with your strides. At your current pace of 10 minutes and 50 seconds per kilometer, try a two-step-in and two-step-out pattern. Inhale as you plant your left foot, exhale as you land on your right, and let that rhythm carry you through the next few hundred metres. Keep it smooth; your heart rate is high at 163 beats per minute, so let your breathing help manage that effort!
